html:
Juan Pablo Duarte was the liberal idealist who founded the secret society La Trinitaria in 1838 to win independence from Haiti. Dominicans honour him as the main founding father of their country.

The son of a Spanish merchant in Santo Domingo, he studied in Europe and came home with ideas of a free republic. He was in exile when the revolt of 1844 began, and on his return the strongman Pedro Santana soon drove him out again.

He offered his services during the Restoration War against Spain but was sidelined. He died poor in Caracas, Venezuela, in 1876. His remains lie in the Altar of the Fatherland in Santo Domingo, the city where Haitian rule ended.
